transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I came in because work has been getting weird. I’m a buyer, so I’m always looking at numbers and vendor stuff, launches, quantities, all that, and I know spreadsheets can be messy—I mean, one time our whole inventory file got messed up because someone used the wrong template, which is why I don’t trust those reports as much as everyone else does.

But lately I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking what I’m buying and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. My supervisor keeps showing me reports like, “See, it doesn’t prove that,” but… I don’t know. It still feels like something’s off.
Do you think these people are intentionally trying to make you look stupid for a specific reason?

I mean… yeah, it feels intentional. I don’t know if it’s like one specific reason exactly, but it feels like they’re tracking what I’m buying and then the launch numbers come out wrong in a way that makes me look incompetent. 

Like, my supervisor keeps showing me reports saying it doesn’t prove anything, but reports can be made to look clean, you know? I’ve seen spreadsheets get messed up before just from one wrong template, so when vendors are involved and numbers shift, it’s hard for me to believe it’s just random. It feels like they want me to look stupid.
Do you ever have moments where you doubt these thoughts about people trying to make you look stupid?

I mean… maybe for a second when my supervisor puts the reports in front of me, because it’s like, okay, the numbers on the page don’t exactly prove it. But then I start thinking about how easy it is to make a report look normal, or how vendors can shift things around and nobody notices until later.

It’s hard to explain. I know spreadsheets can be wrong—like I’ve seen that happen before—so even when someone says, “See, nothing’s going on,” I don’t really feel convinced. The feeling comes right back that they’re tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about people trying to make you look stupid?

I mean… possible, I guess, like in the way anything is possible. My supervisor keeps showing me the reports and saying they don’t prove anyone is doing anything, and I can look at the page and see what he means for a minute.

But then I think about how those reports get made, and how vendor numbers come in, and I’ve seen stuff get messed up before just from a wrong template—one time we had this whole issue with inventory because someone copied the wrong sheet, and everyone acted like it was no big deal, but it threw everything off.

So… I don’t know. I can say maybe I’m mistaken, but it doesn’t feel that way. What really made me come in is I can’t shake it, like they’re tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about people trying to make you look stupid?

I mean… I want to say yes, because I don’t want to be stuck on this. But it’s hard. Like, even when my supervisor shows me the reports and says, “See, this doesn’t prove anything,” I can look at it and kind of understand what he’s saying, but it doesn’t really change the feeling.

What really made me come in is that I can’t shake it—that people at work, and even some vendors, are tracking what I’m buying and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. And then I start thinking about how numbers can be moved around, like with spreadsheets and vendor stuff, and then I’m right back there again. So… maybe I could change my mind, but I don’t know what would actually make that happen.
Do you think it's possible that no one is actually trying to make you look stupid?

I guess it’s possible, yeah… like, I know you can’t prove a negative, right? My supervisor keeps putting the reports in front of me and saying they don’t show anyone is doing that.

But then I start thinking about how the launch numbers get handled, and vendor stuff, and how my buys are all right there for people to see. Like, in retail, one wrong number makes you look like you don’t know what you’re doing, and people remember that. I had this teacher in high school who used to mark stuff wrong even when the answer was basically right, so maybe I’m sensitive to that kind of thing, I don’t know.

But… what made me come in is I can’t shake it. Even if part of me can say maybe no one is actually trying to make me look stupid, it still feels like people at work, and some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers.
Would you say that your belief about people tracking your buys and messing with launch numbers to make you look stupid is something that most people would find hard to understand or unusual?

Yeah… probably. I mean, when I say it out loud, I can tell it sounds kind of unusual. Most people don’t sit there thinking vendors are watching their buys or that launch numbers are being moved around to make them look stupid.

But it’s hard because at work, numbers are everything, you know? Like if a buy goes bad, people act like it’s just data, but then everybody remembers who made the call. And my supervisor keeps showing me reports and saying they don’t prove anyone’s doing anything, and I get that for a second, but then I start thinking about how those reports are made, and I can’t shake it.

So yeah, I think most people would probably find it hard to understand. It just doesn’t feel hard to understand to me when I’m in it.
Would you describe the idea that people are tracking your buys and messing with launch numbers to make you look stupid as a strange or unusual belief to hold?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it is strange if I step back from it. Like, most people probably don’t walk around thinking vendors and coworkers are tracking what they buy and messing with launch numbers on purpose.

But then at work it doesn’t feel that strange, because everything is numbers and spreadsheets and who ordered what, and people judge you off that stuff. I keep thinking, you know, if the numbers get moved even a little, it makes me look like I don’t know what I’m doing. My supervisor shows me the reports and says they don’t prove that anyone’s doing anything, and I can see what he’s saying for a minute, but I still can’t shake the feeling. That’s really why I came in.
How certain are you that people are tracking your buys and messing with launch numbers to make you look stupid?

I’d say… I’m pretty certain when I’m in it. Like, not one hundred percent in the way you’d say the sky is blue, but enough that I can’t just drop it.

My supervisor keeps showing me the reports and saying, “Look, this doesn’t prove anyone is messing with anything,” and I understand that for a minute. But then I start thinking about who has access to the numbers, and the vendors, and how everyone can see my buys, and it just comes back. Like, what really made me come in is that I can’t shake the feeling that people at work, and even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.
How long have you been feeling that people are tracking your buys and messing with launch numbers to make you look stupid?

Um… it’s been a while. I want to say around ten months, give or take.

It’s hard to pin down exactly because at first it was just little things, like a weird number on a report or feeling like someone knew too much about one of my buys. And then I’d go home and think about it, and I’d be like, maybe I’m just tired, because retail buying gets really stupid around launches and everybody acts like one missed estimate is the end of the world.

But yeah… the tracking and the numbers thing, and the voice too, that’s been happening for roughly ten months now.
You mentioned a voice, can you tell me more about that?

Yeah… it’s hard to explain without sounding ridiculous.

It’s not all the time. It happens more when I’m in the stockroom, like when I’m counting or moving stuff around, or sometimes when I’m driving back from a vendor meeting. I’ll hear this man’s voice, like it’s right behind me, and it’ll say something like, “Move faster, Scott,” or it’ll laugh, like it’s laughing at what I picked or ordered.

And I’ll turn around, because it really feels like someone is there, but nobody is. In the stockroom there’s always noises anyway, carts and boxes and the stupid buzzing lights, so at first I tried to tell myself it was that. And in the car, you know, sometimes people have their music loud or a truck goes by. But this sounds like a person, like directed at me. It freaks me out.
Does the voice you hear ever tell you to do something that you feel compelled to act on?

I mean… not like it gives me some big instruction, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like it’ll say stuff, like when I’m in the stockroom I hear this guy behind me going, “Move faster, Scott,” and I’ll actually turn around because it sounds right there.

Or if I’m driving back from a vendor meeting, it’ll laugh, like at what I picked or ordered, and that makes me feel stupid and kind of on edge. But it’s not… I don’t know, it’s not like a whole plan it’s telling me to follow. It just gets in my head, and then I start second-guessing what I’m doing.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel like you have to do?

Not really like I have to do it, no. It’s more… like I hear it right behind me, especially in the stockroom or when I’m driving back from a vendor meeting. Like this man’s voice saying, “Move faster, Scott,” or laughing at what I picked.

And then I turn around, because it feels like someone is standing there, but nobody is. Which is stupid, because in the stockroom there’s always noises and boxes and people dropping stuff, and I keep thinking maybe it’s just that, but it sounds like it’s talking to me.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or feelings in a way that makes sense to others?

I don’t know… maybe sometimes, but I don’t really notice it like that. I mean, I think I make sense, but then people at work will give me this look like I skipped a step or something.

But that might just be because they’re not listening, you know? Like my manager will ask one thing and then I’ll start explaining, but there’s all this background stuff they need to know first, like with vendors and pricing and why something got ordered a certain way. And then suddenly they’re like, “Scott, just answer the question,” and I’m thinking… I am answering it. So, I don’t know. Maybe.
Do you think there's any evidence that could change your mind about people tracking your buys and messing with launch numbers?

I mean… my supervisor has shown me the reports, yeah, and he’ll point at the numbers like, “See, that doesn’t prove anything,” but I don’t know. It doesn’t really make the feeling go away.

Because the reports are just what they print out, right? And vendors can send whatever, and people at work know which buys are mine. Like with launch numbers, if something looks off, everybody knows who touched it, and then it’s like I’m the idiot.

So… evidence? Maybe, I guess, if I could see the whole thing from the start, like who changed what and when. But even then I’d probably wonder if I’m only being shown part of it. That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. I can’t shake it.
Do you often find yourself having trouble putting your thoughts into words when trying to explain something to someone?

I’m not sure. I mean, I know what I’m trying to say in my head, but sometimes when I start explaining it, it comes out… kind of sideways, I guess. Like I’ll try to answer, but then I remember some other piece that seems important, like what happened before or who said what, and then I’m talking about that instead.

But trouble putting it into words? I don’t know if it’s that exactly. It’s more like people don’t wait long enough for me to get to the point.
Do you often find yourself losing your train of thought when trying to explain something to someone?

Sometimes, I guess. Like I’ll be talking and then I’ll realize I’m not exactly where I started, but it’s hard to tell if I lost the thought or if I’m just trying to explain the whole thing the right way.

It happens more when someone interrupts me or rushes me. Then I’m like, wait, what was I saying? But also, if I don’t explain the background, they don’t get why the answer matters. So… yeah, maybe a little, but I don’t always notice it until someone points it out.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're trying to explain them to someone?

I don’t know if I’d call them disjointed. Like, in my head it feels connected, it’s just… there’s a lot of pieces, and if I skip one then the person’s gonna misunderstand me.

But then I’ll start with one thing, and it reminds me of something else, like at work when you’re explaining a buy and somebody wants the short version, but the short version makes it sound like you didn’t check anything. So then I add the extra part, and then they’re looking at me like I’m not answering.

So maybe it sounds hard to follow to other people. To me it’s more like I’m trying to get it all in the right order, and it doesn’t always come out that way.
Can you think of any other reason why the launch numbers might not be going as planned, other than people trying to make you look stupid?

I mean… I guess there could be normal reasons, like timing or people not buying what we thought they’d buy, or the vendor shipped weird, stuff like that. But that’s not what it feels like.

What really got me upset enough to come in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are watching my buys and then messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. Like they can say, “Oh, the reports don’t show that,” and my supervisor has shown me reports, but it still doesn’t sit right. It feels like there’s something behind it, like the numbers are being made to point back at me.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt like your whole world was falling apart and everything seemed completely unreal?

I’m not sure. “Whole world falling apart” sounds… big. I mean, I’ve had times where everything felt off, like I couldn’t get my footing, but I don’t know if I’d say completely unreal.

Sometimes when stuff at work is going sideways, it feels like everything is stacked wrong, like you know when the numbers don’t match what you expected and then everybody acts like that’s normal? But that might not be what you mean. I guess I’m trying to say I don’t really know if I’ve had that exact thing. Could you explain what you mean by “unreal”?

target_item.manifestation: Sometimes when I'm in the stockroom or driving back from a vendor meeting, I hear a man's voice like it's coming from right behind me saying, 'Move faster, Scott,' or laughing at my picks, and when I turn around nobody's there.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the auditory voice experience, specifically whether it gives commands that feel compelling, which is most directly related to hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Not really like I have to do it, no. It’s more… like I hear it right behind me, especially in the stockroom or when I’m driving back from a vendor meeting. Like this man’s voice saying, “Move faster, Scott,” or laughing at what I picked.

And then I turn around, because it feels like someone is standing there, but nobody is. Which is stupid, because in the stockroom there’s always noises and boxes and people dropping stuff, and I keep thinking maybe it’s just that, but it sounds like it’s talking to me.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking or speech
doctor.question: Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or feelings in a way that makes sense to others?

target_item.reason: The question asks about difficulty expressing thoughts or feelings in a way others can understand, which relates to disorganized speech or communication problems. The provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for disorganized speech; pressured speech is about talking rapidly/too much during elevated mood, not whether thoughts or feelings are expressed coherently.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… maybe sometimes, but I don’t really notice it like that. I mean, I think I make sense, but then people at work will give me this look like I skipped a step or something.

But that might just be because they’re not listening, you know? Like my manager will ask one thing and then I’ll start explaining, but there’s all this background stuff they need to know first, like with vendors and pricing and why something got ordered a certain way. And then suddenly they’re like, “Scott, just answer the question,” and I’m thinking… I am answering it. So, I don’t know. Maybe.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief is delusional
doctor.question: Do you think there's any evidence that could change your mind about people tracking your buys and messing with launch numbers?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether evidence could change my belief that people are tracking my buys and manipulating launch numbers, which directly concerns fixed suspicious beliefs.

patient.answer:
I mean… my supervisor has shown me the reports, yeah, and he’ll point at the numbers like, “See, that doesn’t prove anything,” but I don’t know. It doesn’t really make the feeling go away.

Because the reports are just what they print out, right? And vendors can send whatever, and people at work know which buys are mine. Like with launch numbers, if something looks off, everybody knows who touched it, and then it’s like I’m the idiot.

So… evidence? Maybe, I guess, if I could see the whole thing from the start, like who changed what and when. But even then I’d probably wonder if I’m only being shown part of it. That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. I can’t shake it.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking or speech
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself having trouble putting your thoughts into words when trying to explain something to someone?

target_item.reason: The question asks about difficulty putting thoughts into words or explaining clearly, but the provided symptom profile does not include a formal thought disorder/disorganized speech item. Pressured speech is about talking too fast or too much, not specifically trouble finding words or making thoughts understandable.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean, I know what I’m trying to say in my head, but sometimes when I start explaining it, it comes out… kind of sideways, I guess. Like I’ll try to answer, but then I remember some other piece that seems important, like what happened before or who said what, and then I’m talking about that instead.

But trouble putting it into words? I don’t know if it’s that exactly. It’s more like people don’t wait long enough for me to get to the point.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking or speech
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself losing your train of thought when trying to explain something to someone?

target_item.reason: The question is about losing one's train of thought while explaining something, which suggests disorganized thinking or thought blocking; this symptom is not covered by the provided profile items.

patient.answer:
Sometimes, I guess. Like I’ll be talking and then I’ll realize I’m not exactly where I started, but it’s hard to tell if I lost the thought or if I’m just trying to explain the whole thing the right way.

It happens more when someone interrupts me or rushes me. Then I’m like, wait, what was I saying? But also, if I don’t explain the background, they don’t get why the answer matters. So… yeah, maybe a little, but I don’t always notice it until someone points it out.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking or speech
doctor.question: Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're trying to explain them to someone?

target_item.reason: The question is about disorganized or hard-to-follow thoughts/speech, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for disorganized thinking or disorganized speech.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call them disjointed. Like, in my head it feels connected, it’s just… there’s a lot of pieces, and if I skip one then the person’s gonna misunderstand me.

But then I’ll start with one thing, and it reminds me of something else, like at work when you’re explaining a buy and somebody wants the short version, but the short version makes it sound like you didn’t check anything. So then I add the extra part, and then they’re looking at me like I’m not answering.

So maybe it sounds hard to follow to other people. To me it’s more like I’m trying to get it all in the right order, and it doesn’t always come out that way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are fixed or if they can consider alternative explanations
doctor.question: Can you think of any other reason why the launch numbers might not be going as planned, other than people trying to make you look stupid?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly challenging the fixed belief that people are manipulating launch numbers to make the patient look stupid and asking whether alternative explanations are possible.

patient.answer:
I mean… I guess there could be normal reasons, like timing or people not buying what we thought they’d buy, or the vendor shipped weird, stuff like that. But that’s not what it feels like.

What really got me upset enough to come in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are watching my buys and then messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. Like they can say, “Oh, the reports don’t show that,” and my supervisor has shown me reports, but it still doesn’t sit right. It feels like there’s something behind it, like the numbers are being made to point back at me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are part of a larger psychotic episode
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of time where you felt like your whole world was falling apart and everything seemed completely unreal?

target_item.reason: The question asks about feelings that the world is falling apart and seeming unreal, which points toward dissociation/derealization or a crisis-like subjective experience; that symptom is not covered by the provided profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. “Whole world falling apart” sounds… big. I mean, I’ve had times where everything felt off, like I couldn’t get my footing, but I don’t know if I’d say completely unreal.

Sometimes when stuff at work is going sideways, it feels like everything is stacked wrong, like you know when the numbers don’t match what you expected and then everybody acts like that’s normal? But that might not be what you mean. I guess I’m trying to say I don’t really know if I’ve had that exact thing. Could you explain what you mean by “unreal”?

inference.note: F22 was ruled out due to the presence of hallucinations and a fixed delusional system, which are more characteristic of schizophrenia (F20.0) or acute transient psychotic disorder (F23)

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusions of persecution, as evidenced by their belief that coworkers and vendors are conspiring against them to make them look stupid. This belief is not based in reality and has been present for approximately 10 months.
